title: Subprogram tasks
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming 2: data structures, files and subprograms
source: Seeded from computing/y10 lesson 33 (Pupil PDF worksheet: subprogram tasks)
intro: Lesson 33: Subprograms: functions, procedures and parameters. To understand how functions and procedures with parameters make programs shorter, clearer and reusable

questions.q: Write a function vat(price) that returns the price plus 20% VAT. Call it with 50.
questions.a: def vat(price): return price * 1.2 → vat(50) returns 60.0
questions.model: I do: def vat(price): then return price * 1.2. Main program: total = vat(50); print(total) shows 60.0.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: write a function average(numbers) that returns the mean of a list, and a procedure report(name, numbers) that prints the name and average. Test with [62, 75, 48, 90].
questions.a: average returns 68.75; report prints the name and 68.75.
questions.model: The teacher writes the header: def average(numbers): total = 0; for n in numbers: total = total + n; return total / len(numbers)

questions.q: Extend: give two benefits of subprograms.
questions.a: Code reuse; easier testing and debugging; clearer structure.

questions.q: Stretch: what is printed? def f(x): x = x + 1; return x then a = 5; f(a); print(a)
questions.a: 5: the function's change is local and the return value was not stored.

questions.q: A variable created inside a function is ...
Back to our ponder: If you needed the same ten lines of code in five places, what could go wrong if you copied them each time?
questions.a: A fix must be made five times and mistakes creep in; a subprogram is written once and called many times.
